Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`), single Proxmox host, real production system.

## The ask

The owner wants a unified, real-time operations monitor in the admin portal — one place to see live activity across EVERY server the platform runs (VPS, shared hosting, game servers): traffic, actions, connections. Explicit request: "a visual terminal UX/UI" — a console/NOC aesthetic, not typical dashboard cards.

## What already exists — read this first, this is a v1 built ON TOP of real infra, not from scratch

- **Per-server console access already exists and is real**: `lib/terminal-token.ts` (JWE-encrypted access tickets, mirrors a VNC console ticket system), noVNC in-browser console, and a web terminal — check how these actually connect (likely a WebSocket proxy to each VM's console/shell). This is PER-SERVER (one customer/admin looking at ONE VM). The new ask is the opposite: ALL servers, aggregated, one view — but the terminal aesthetic and any WebSocket plumbing here is worth reusing/matching rather than reinventing.
- **Periodic resource sampling already exists**: `worker/monitor.ts`, `lib/node-capacity.ts`, `ServerDiskSample` (check `prisma/schema.prisma`) — this is what already produces the "Capacity warnings — hosting-1 DISK 83%" admin alert. Read this fully; it's your best source for what data is ALREADY being collected platform-wide (CPU/disk/memory samples per server/node) that a monitor view can display without inventing new collection.
- **`Job` table**: every provisioning/power/backup/etc. action across every server already gets a row here (`type`, `status`, `attempts`, `progress`, `step`, `serverId`, timestamps) — this is a real, ready-made "recent actions across all servers" feed with zero new instrumentation needed.
- Check for any existing connection/traffic-level data: `worker/hosting.ts`, `worker/game-control.ts`, `lib/nat-rules.ts`/NAT rule counters, any bandwidth/network sampling already happening (`ServerDiskSample` might be disk-only — check if there's a bandwidth equivalent, or if this needs new collection).

## What to build (v1 — foundational, not the final word, same philosophy as the accounting/provision-health work done today)

1. A new admin page — check `lib/admin-groups.ts`'s `fleet` group for where this sensibly lives (near Servers/Infrastructure/Operations), add a nav entry (e.g. "Monitor" or "Live Ops").
2. A genuine terminal/console-styled UI: monospace type, dark ground, scrolling log-line aesthetic for the activity feed (recent Job rows across ALL servers, formatted like log lines — timestamp, server, action, status), NOT a grid-of-cards dashboard. Use your judgment on how far to push the aesthetic, but it should read as a console, not a SaaS dashboard reskinned.
3. Real, live-updating data: aggregate resource state (CPU/disk/memory, from whatever `worker/monitor.ts` already samples) across every server, grouped/filterable by type (VPS, shared hosting, game servers). Poll-based auto-refresh is a legitimate v1 (don't over-build a WebSocket push system for this unless the existing terminal-token/console infra makes it genuinely easy to reuse — check first, don't build new WS plumbing from scratch if it's a bigger lift than it's worth for v1).
4. Recent-actions feed: the last N `Job` rows across all servers (not just one), live-updating, showing what's actually happening platform-wide right now (a provision running, a backup completing, a power action, etc.).
5. If genuine live network/connection data isn't already being collected anywhere (check thoroughly first), don't fabricate it — either note it as a real v2 gap (this platform doesn't currently sample live connection counts/bandwidth per server) rather than faking a number, or if it's a small, clean addition to the existing `worker/monitor.ts` sampling loop, add it for real.

## Ground rules

- Real data only — every number/line shown must trace back to something genuinely happening on the platform. No fabricated traffic graphs or placeholder activity.
- `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-livemonitor -b feature/live-server-monitor`, symlink only `.env`, real `node_modules` via `npm ci`. Check `df -h /` first — if under 5GB free, stop and report. Delete your worktree's `node_modules`/`.next` once committed (hard requirement — a real disk-full production incident happened today from worktrees left with these).
- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean.
- If this needs a schema change (e.g. a new sampling table), keep it additive-only, write the manual migration SQL matching today's established convention (`prisma/manual-migration-*.sql`), and do NOT run `prisma db push` against any live database — commit and hold for review, same as every other schema-touching change today.
- Commit your work but do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging or production. Stop after committing and report back.

Report back: what real data sources you wired in (and what, if anything, doesn't exist yet and would need real new collection), how "live" the view actually is (polling interval, or genuine WebSocket push if you found a clean way to reuse existing infra), a description of the actual visual design (this is real UI/UX work, describe what you built, not just "a page"), the commit hash, and confirmation of disk cleanup.
